thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 HIGH: hosted-api us-west-2 — request queue growth observed, autoscaler failing to provision GPUs. Paging oncall.

sara: i'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 6s -> p95 18s in the last 5m, p99 ~ 42s. some requests timing out. queue depth jumping from 200 -> 1.8k in 10m.

dan: confirmed. autoscaler logs show repeated `Instance create rate limit exceeded` errors around 15:12 UTC. Provider 429s on instance create.

tim: FYI this looks like a quota/rate-limit at the cloud infra level. we hit burst provisioning cap. fallback pools are empty.

sara: routing policy still pinned to high-capacity gpu pools. we need immediate mitigations: 1) enable lighter-model routing (cpu/quantized) 2) apply temporary global rate limit 3) kick off emergency reserved pool.

nisha: @sara i'll flip lighter-model routing now. will route non-critical traffic to gpt-small-quantized variant (same API surface). doing a canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

sara: copy. @tim can you open support case with provider and request quota surge? include request IDs from `autoscaler` logs: create_err_17221, create_err_17222.

tim: on it. raising support + escalation. ETA 20-30m if they approve surge. also creating cloud-provider ticket: CP-894213.

oncall-infra: I've added a temporary soft quota bump on our reserved pools (50 GPUs) but provisioning takes time. we should also consider eviction policy to free ephemeral capacity.

cs-tilly: alert from customer A: several requests returned 503 at 15:17. Customer success flagged a major customer chat flow failing. They need an incident summary.

sara: noted. i'll draft impact blurb. Short: "users may see increased latency or 503s between 15:10-ongoing in us-west-2. We're routing to lighter models and escalated provisioning."

deploy-bot: deployment 2026.03.15-991 promoted to hosted us-west-2 at 15:08 UTC (image: runtime-v2.4.1).

dan: logs show high tail latency is due to large-batch inference requests that aren't being cached. a bunch of clients sending long sequences concurrently. p50 token generation time healthy, but p99 token time is spiking due to KV cache misses and no batching.

sara: let's enable prefix caching (hot prefixes) for the next 30m for chat sessions. @tim can you toggle caching policy to aggressive for us-west?

tim: toggled prefix cache TTL -> 10m and aggressive caching on. should reduce downstream tokens by ~20% for repeated prompts.

nisha: lighter-model routing at 40% now. early signs: queue dropping from 1800 -> 980 in 4m, p95 down to 12s. routing metrics: error rate for rerouted requests ~1.2% (format mismatches), we'll capture and auto-fallback those.

sara: good. enable "fallback to small" for failed conversions to avoid 503 cascades.

oncall-infra: autoscaler still returning create errors; provider hasn't approved surge yet. we'll start evicting low-priority batch jobs from dedicated pools to reclaim ~24 GPUs. scheduling eviction now.

dan: evictions started. observed immediate drop in queue depth by ~250. p99 trending down, currently ~30s. still some stuck long-running requests timing out at load balancer (504). we should extend lb timeout temporarily to 90s while cleanup continues.

sara: changed LB timeout to 90s for the region. also enabling per-customer throttles: customers above baseline QPS will be limited to prevent single-tenant stomps.

cs-tilly: customer A reported recovery for chat loop after 15:26. still monitoring. they asked for root cause and ETA for full restoration.

sara: immediate mitigation list: - lighter-model routing (done) - prefix cache aggressive (done) - evict low-priority batch (in progress) - extend LB timeout (done) - open provider support (in progress) - per-tenant throttles (done)

nisha: metrics update at 15:38: queue = 480, p95 = 9s, p99 = 18s, error-rate = 0.9%. token spend per request down 17% due to caching + small-model routing.

tim: support replied: they won't allow additional instances under burst policy for 30m; recommending spreading provisioning across regions. we can't shift stateful pinned reservations quickly.

sara: action: prepare post-incident communication. collect affected customers, timeline, and mitigations. assign postmortem to @dan and @nisha. incident severity: Sev2 (partial outage for some customers in us-west-2).

dan: will own postmortem. logs and metrics snapshots saved to /incidents/3079999999/artifacts. will include autoscaler request IDs, provider responses, and recommendations (regional failover, slower client-side backoff, reserve small burst capacity).

sara: thanks all. oncall handoff to @tim at 16:00 UTC. @tim please confirm once monitoring stable for 30m and then close the pager.

oncall-infra: handoff acknowledged. monitoring window started 15:44 UTC. will call if regressions.

cs-tilly: i've notified impacted customers and set expectation: full mitigation in progress; follow-up with root cause and timeline within 4 hours.

incident-bot: MONITORING -> no new severity changes. thread will be archived when closed.

sara: summary note to put in postmortem: primary failure mode = cloud provider instance create rate limits during sudden burst; secondary = pinned routing to capacity-heavy pools without regional fallback. mitigations executed: fallback routing, prefix caching, evictions, LB timeout increase, per-tenant throttles. recommended long-term: pre-warm reserve capacity, multi-region automatic failover, autoscaler backoff/queue smoothing, and client-side guidance for exponential retry/backoff.

tim: monitoring green at 16:14 UTC, queue stable < 200, p99 < 10s. closing pager in 30m if no regressions.

sara: thanks team. will kick off postmortem doc and owner assignment in ~1h.
